title: Role Strains and How Working Students Cope with Them
summary:
Background: Many students work while pursuing their studies. As a result, they must juggle the demands of both their academic and professional lives simultaneously. This can lead to time pressures and increased stress. To date, there have been relatively few studies on the specific stressors faced by students who work while studying. This study therefore aims to contribute to a better understanding of the stress experienced by this group of individuals.
Research Question: The study examines whether and how personal and social resources that students use to cope with demands are related to the extent of their perceived stress resulting from the simultaneous demands of their studies and work. In addition, correlations with perceived quality of life as well as their own work and academic performance are examined.
Methodology: The study will be conducted as a one-time online survey. Students will be asked about their academic and work situations, as well as their perceived stress and how they cope with these demands. Additionally, questions will be asked about quality of life and their own work and academic performance. The responses will then be statistically analyzed to investigate possible correlations between the various areas.

interventions.name:
Working students are surveyed once on the following topics:
- Role strain (based on the Job Caregiver Role Strain Scale; Beitman et al., 2004; Bohen & Viveros-Long, 1981)
- Coping resources (FMaW; Wienert, 2011)
- Health-related quality of life (WHOQOL-BREF; WHO, 2020)
- Subjective work ability

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Enrollment in at least the second semester of a degree program
- Willingness and personal ability to participate in the online survey
- Current paid employment alongside studies
Exclusion criteria:
- Underage
- Enrolled in the first semester of a degree program
- Lack of subjective ability to participate in the survey
- No current paid employment alongside studies
